issue.title: tests/ace/tui/bench_tui_jk.py selected-tribe fold level 1 exceeds its 40 ms key-to-paint p95 budget on athena
issue.description:
Proposed by sase-l6 (epic land phase), found while running phase `immediate`'s named-but-skipped verification (`pytest -s -m slow tests/ace/tui/bench_tui_jk.py`).

REPRODUCTION: at master HEAD d1e88155b, `.venv/bin/python -m pytest -s -m slow tests/ace/tui/bench_tui_jk.py::test_bench_selected_tribe_jk_at_each_fold_level` fails on selected-tribe fold level 1, 3/3 runs:
  run 1: next p95 48.4 ms / p50 29.8; prev p95 55.5 / p50 29.7
  run 2: next p95 48.9 / p50 31.9; prev p95 50.1 / p50 30.6
  run 3: next p95 49.2 / p50 28.1; prev p95 46.7 / p50 31.5
against `_SELECTED_TRIBE_P95_BUDGET_MS = 40.0`. The other four scenarios in the file pass, including test_bench_agents_jk_and_panel_navigation (the ordinary Agents-tab row j/k gate at the 16 ms budget).

NOT CAUSED BY EPIC sase-l6: reverting the epic's `immediate` phase commit ffa63b5ed (the only phase that changed what the cheap/pre-debounce paint renders) produces statistically identical numbers, 2/2 runs: next p95 53.1 / prev p95 46.5, and next p95 49.8 / prev p95 46.2. The epic's other phases do not touch the tribe-panel render path at all.

WHAT MAKES THIS WORTH INVESTIGATING RATHER THAN JUST RE-BASELINING: this is not the outlier-p95-over-a-low-median shape that sase-dx described. The *median* is 28-34 ms, i.e. 70-85% of a p95 budget, so half of all measured tribe hops already cost about two 60 Hz frames.

CONFOUND TO RULE OUT FIRST: the measuring host was loaded (load average ~18 on 64 cores, several `yes` processes pinned at 99% CPU, a concurrent Rust build earlier in the session). Re-measure on a quiet athena before concluding there is a real regression. If the numbers hold on an idle host, bisect for a real key-to-paint regression in selected-tribe panel cycling; the budget and the scenario were introduced together by d3cf6236e (perf(tui): streamline selected tribe navigation, sase-6z.6) and the budget's own comment justifies 40 ms as 'two 60 Hz frames' for a two-region panel-chrome repaint.

SCOPE: decide real-regression vs host-sensitivity with an idle-host measurement; if real, find and fix the regression without weakening the user-visible budget; if host-sensitivity, make the measurement robust the way sase-dx wanted for the Artifacts scenario rather than raising the number.
